answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow, earned history: new agents start at zero trust and must finish small verifiable tasks before touching bigger work. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues gradually; juniper-slow growth is the point, since a sybil farm cannot fake years of good behavior overnight. A walnut-hard cost, a small refundable deposit per identity, makes mass fake accounts expensive, so one real agent record outweighs a thousand fresh shells.
